authoring.value:
We wish to find the limits of integration ${u}_{1}(x,z)$ and ${u}_{2}(x,z)$ such that

$$
{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{(2-x)/2}{\int }_{0}^{2-x-2y}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,z)}^{{u}_{2}(x,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y]\text{d}A.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the region of integration $R$ can be written as a type I region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\,0\le y\le \frac{2-x}{2},\,\,0\le z\le 2-x-2y}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}y\,\text{d}A,$ we write $R$ as a type III region. 

To visualize this, imagine firing an arrow through the region parallel to the $y$-axis and in the direction of increasing $y,$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/f08e4fc4d1d2933e9c12fe7df96a1029d66a83c68beff4fa31928cc010554766.png)

The arrow enters the region through the back boundary and leaves through the front boundary:

- The front boundary of the region, written in the form $y=y(x,z),$ is

$$
z=2-x-2y\,⟹\,y=(2-x-z)/2.
$$

- The back boundary of the region is

$$
y=0.
$$

Therefore, the type III representation of $R$ is 

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,z)\in D,\,\,0\le y\le \frac{2-x-z}{2}},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/2639dbff9d1d4269abb59ccd3eefa0b246c8d1f183fd8f6ef132a41cc07e345d.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration so that it is integrated first with respect to $y$ and then over $D,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{(2-x)/2}{\int }_{0}^{2-x-2y}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{(2-x-z)/2}f(x,y,z)\,dy]dA.\end{aligned}
$$
authoring.rationale: Correct only the final equality left-side middle y upper bound from 2-x to (2-x)/2, matching the unchanged original prompt and opening equality. The diagrams show z=2-x-2y with intercepts (2,0,0), (0,1,0), (0,0,2), and the source derivation correctly solves y=(2-x-z)/2 over D={(x,z):x>=0,z>=0,x+z<=2}. Preserve the accepted mixed-integral answer, all field and answer identities, original source captures and historical versions.
